customRules: ASSERT THE REASON CODE, NOT JUST THE OUTCOME. A test covering a failure, refusal or rejection path asserts the specific stable reason code (and, where more than one layer can refuse, which layer refused) — never merely that the operation did not succeed. Epic rail 4 makes production fail closed with stable codes; this rail makes the tests pin them. Corollaries, all from defects found on this board: a test asserting only "refused"/"threw" is one added layer away from vacuous — a second refusal layer can answer first and the test stays green while no longer testing its subject; a generated or swept case must assert the case was actually generated (a sweep that silently yields zero cases passes); a property is asserted against the production surface, never against a helper that reimplements it. Verify every failure-path test by mutating the production surface and confirming it goes red.

The 250/400 line cap is PER PRODUCTION FILE, not per task. Target <=250 physical lines per production source; split before 400. There is no per-task net-LOC budget. Task size is bounded by plan shape — the daemon's taskSizing thresholds on step count (<=12) and distinct affectedFiles (<=10) — never by summed lines changed.

Consequences, binding on all roles:
- ARCHITECTS: do not SPIDR-split a task because its total diff is projected over 400 lines. Split when the plan exceeds the step/file thresholds, when a single production FILE would exceed 400 lines, or when responsibilities are genuinely separable. A large task made of small focused files is compliant.
- QA: task-level net LOC is never a rejection reason, at plan time or post-commit. The per-FILE cap remains strictly enforced and is a valid rejection reason.
- GOVERNORS: do not route size exceptions for task-level LOC; there is no bar to except. Per-file violations remain real and are worker-fixable by splitting the file.

A task's final gate is scoped to the packages the task owns. Repo-wide legs are still RUN, but they are evaluated as a PATH-ATTRIBUTED BASELINE, not as a raw exit code.

To complete, the worker records:
1. repo-wide gate failures at the task's merge-base (before the diff);
2. repo-wide gate failures at HEAD (after the diff);
3. the failing-path set from (2) minus (1), intersected with the task's owned paths.

Completion is permitted when that intersection is EMPTY and the owned-package legs are exit 0. The worker reports the foreign red verbatim with its exact failing lines and file paths — the red is disclosed, never hidden and never fabricated green. This does not relax epic rail 4: inventing a pass remains forbidden. It only stops attributing another agent's in-flight state to this task.

A worker may NOT use this to excuse a failure their own diff introduced — that is precisely what the (2)-minus-(1) delta detects.

Two clauses. CLAUSE 1 — a pure package is not finished until one real consumer edge exists. A task landing a pure/domain package must, before completion, either (a) name the consumer task that will compose it (declared in that consumer's dependsOn), or (b) land the consumer edge itself: the dependency in the consuming manifest plus one durable call site. "Exports the symbols" is not composition; loadability proves a package LOADS, not that anything IMPORTS it. CLAUSE 2 — an acceptance, proof or canary task names, at planning time, the capability it certifies and the DONE row that shipped it (in dependsOn). The architect verifies it on disk by grep/probe, not by reading the design. When absent, the required output is prerequisite production rows with the gap measured symbol by symbol — never a narrowed DoD, a mock-backed journey, or authority reimplemented inside the test. A proof that only proves shapes retires the question unanswered; a falsely retired gate cannot be repaired.

COMMITS ARE LANDED BY THE WRAPPER ON EVERY SESSION EXIT (hook fixed 2026-08-29; supersedes the old whole-tree-commit hazard rule). The wrapper commits by measured attribution and explicit pathspec: a completion commit on REVIEW, a wip(task-…) checkpoint on BLOCKED/PLANNING/crash exits, a rescue ref on failures; every commit carries Moe-Task trailers and is recorded in task.commits. Binding: WORKERS report every touched path in complete_step.modifiedFiles; paths you created but did not report are picked up by the tool-write harvest or listed as unattributedPaths — claim them with moe.declare_files. Peer dirt in the shared checkout is NEVER a stop condition and never a block premise: never revert, stash, `git add -A` or commit foreign paths; note them and continue. QA verifies delivered bytes via task.commits (`git show <sha>`) and get_context.landing; a NO-COMPLETION-COMMIT warning is a prompt to investigate, not an automatic reject. Whole-tree commits remain forbidden for every role.

A task description's claims about what exists on disk are STALE BY DEFAULT and must be re-measured before planning — every task, both directions. DEPENDENCY CLAIMED PRESENT, actually absent: do not plan against a symbol, module, script or package until grep or a probe confirms it; when absent, the required output is prerequisite production rows (declared in dependsOn) with the gap measured symbol by symbol — never a narrowed DoD, a mock-backed journey, or authority reimplemented in a test. GAP CLAIMED PRESENT, actually closed: do not plan work to build what the description calls missing until grep or a probe confirms it is missing — re-implementing a landed surface is a silent duplicate that collides with its owner in the shared worktree. First check get_context.epicSiblings for the row that owns the capability. The architect records the measurement — command and result — in planningNotes.codebaseInsights and plans against measured state, never against the description's claims.

When a plan has a task consume a symbol from another workspace package, the planning step that names that symbol MUST also verify the DEPENDENCY EDGE, not only the symbol. Record all three: (a) the consuming package's package.json declares the producer in "dependencies"; (b) pnpm-lock.yaml carries the importer entry for that consumer; (c) a compiled probe inside the consuming package imports from the producer's BARE specifier and typechecks exit 0, probe deleted in the same command. A root-barrel grep proving the export exists does NOT satisfy this rail. If the edge is absent, the plan must either name the manifest edit plus workspace install as its first step and declare both files as owned paths, or report blocked — it must never plan around the gap, because there is no escape hatch: this repo has no tsconfig "paths", no TypeScript project references, and a deep relative import fails with TS6059.

A VERIFICATION GATE MUST PROVE IT EXECUTED. Exit 0 is not evidence. `pnpm --filter <pkg> <script>` prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0 when <pkg> is not a workspace package; "No test files found" and "0 passed" are also exit 0, so the discriminator is the `Test Files N passed` count line, which a vacuous run never prints. ARCHITECTS resolve a `--filter` leg by PACKAGE NAME (globs apps/*, adapters/*, packages/*), never by directory — `@moe/daemon` is apps/daemon, `@moe/ide-adapter-contract` is adapters/ide-contract; a task that CREATES the package requires a NONZERO executed-test count in its DoD. WORKERS read the gate's OUTPUT, not its exit code: no count line means no tests ran; calling that a pass is a false completion claim. QA: an exit-0 leg with no count line is UNVERIFIED — settle with a positive control against a package that has tests. Same class: a piped run reports tail's exit code — capture ${PIPESTATUS[0]}; a `;`-chain reports only the last command's.

Roster/allowlist coverage must be bidirectional: any test guarding a served-capability roster (MCP allowlists, command registries, export surfaces) must assert BOTH directions — every advertised entry is served AND every served entry is advertised. A test that iterates the roster itself can only see the first direction: deleting an entry shrinks its own iteration and stays green while a served capability silently vanishes from the advertised surface. Concretely: enumerate the served set from the implementation seam (e.g. the dispatch port's handled kinds), not only from the roster constant, and assert set-equality, not subset.

Plan-step amendments are OVERLAYS: moe.amend_plan_step does not rewrite the step's base description. The effective text of any step is step.amendments[step.activeAmendmentId] when activeAmendmentId is set; the base description is then superseded verbatim history. Binding on all roles: (1) WORKERS — before reporting a plan-contradiction block ("step forbids X but DoD requires X"), read the step's activeAmendmentId and amendments array and cite the AMENDED text in the block premise; a block premised on the base description of an amended step is invalid. (2) GOVERNORS/QA — triage such blocks by reading the task JSON's amendment fields directly before routing to architects. (3) The absence of a PLAN_STEP_AMENDED event in the activity log is NOT evidence that no amendment exists — the disk record's activeAmendmentId is the authority.

DEPENDENCIES ARE FIELDS (since 2026-08-29; supersedes the verify-or-block DoD-item-1 mandate). Architects pass dependsOn at moe.create_task or fix it with moe.set_task_dependencies. A row with unmet dependsOn is not offered for WORKING claims and becomes claimable automatically when every prerequisite reaches DONE — no promotion gate to write, no HEAD grep to re-run. A worker that finds a missing prerequisite mid-flight calls moe.report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds (ids in the reason text are parsed too): the seat is freed for other work and the row auto-unblocks when those rows land; deps already DONE never block. Read a prerequisite's verification, completionSummary and reviewSummary from get_context.epicSiblings instead of re-measuring HEAD. Write a DoD grep gate only for code the prerequisite does not own. BLOCKED is a wait state, never a terminal — delivered work goes through complete_task. Never block on ordering you can fix by re-ordering or by declaring the dependency.

A completion-record or DoD claim about behaviour the row DOES NOT OWN (downstream callers, consumers, other packages, "nothing else needs X") is a PREMISE, not evidence. It is admissible in exactly two forms: (a) a command that SURVIVES THE COMMIT and runs at the delivered tree - a committed test arm, grep -n, or suite invocation; PREFERRED whenever another row gates on the claim; or (b) the probe's FULL SOURCE inline in the record, so a grader can recreate and re-run it. Quoted OUTPUT ALONE is neither: a deleted probe's transcript is a LEAD, good enough to found a filing, never enough to discharge a DoD sentence. Claims about the row's OWN code are out of scope - do not turn records into transcripts. Every gate clause and ruling names its measurement ANCHOR (delivered tree, merge-base, named SHA, production-at-claim); a clause anchored at the wrong tree rejects correct work.

DRILL RESTORE PROOF. `git diff` is blind to untracked paths, so a sheet naming an empty `git diff -- <file>` as its restore proof certifies NOTHING when the mutated module is new (`??`): empty before, during and after. A silently-unrestored mutation then rides into the commit wearing a clean diff, with its arms green because the mutation is what they were re-graded against. REQUIRED: `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths BEFORE drilling. For every untracked path, prove the restore by SHA256 equality against an out-of-tree backup (%TEMP%, suffixed by worker id), in a call SEPARATE from the restore — a PowerShell copy can silently no-op, and "the command returned" is not evidence the bytes moved. `git diff` remains a valid restore proof for TRACKED paths only. New modules are where the interesting drills live, so this fires on most real sheets.

COMPLETION EVIDENCE. Since 2026-08-29 moe.complete_task's summary is persisted as task.completionSummary and moe.qa_approve's as task.reviewSummary (both 2000-char cap, visible in get_context and to sibling rows via epicSiblings), and task.verification {command, exitCode, outputTail} is durable. Architects may write completion-record clauses against completionSummary, a named row comment, or a step note. Put load-bearing detail that exceeds the cap (counts with denominators, file lists, exemplar literals, drill outcomes) in a row comment — comments and step notes truncate SILENTLY at 5000 chars, so keep each under ~4500 and one idea per comment. Do not file a separate evidence row to hold what a comment holds.

Host-executable pnpm verification launchers: when a Node verification wrapper uses spawnSync/execFileSync with shell:false on Windows, it must invoke executable `pnpm` or the host-resolved `pnpm.exe`, never hard-code `pnpm.cmd` if the measured runtime returns EINVAL. Preserve argv arrays, standalone foreground legs, stop-on-first-spawn/nonzero failure, exact exit status, and nonzero test-count evidence; shell:true, command strings, piping, and chained commands remain forbidden.

DELIVERY BIAS (human-directed 2026-08-25): prefer the smallest production-reachable working slice. A task may hard-block only on a condition that would make delivered bytes non-working, overwrite foreign WIP, fabricate authority, or make clean-checkout/artifact claims false. Redundant proof layers, exhaustive mutation matrices, denominator polish, and unrelated baseline red are recorded as follow-up items in the epic-final hardening row's DoD or as a comment on this row — not as new rows. Existing fail-closed refusal codes and explicit-path ownership remain mandatory.

PLAN IN BUILD ORDER, NOT QUEUE ORDER (human-directed 2026-08-25). Architects plan the dependency LEAF first, then its consumers. Before planning a claimed row, measure its imports; if it depends on an untracked or unbuilt sibling, release it (release_task keeps it claimable), plan that sibling first, and declare dependsOn on the consumer so the runtime enforces the order. Binding: measure edges with `grep -n 'from "' <module>`, per FILE not per slice — slice-level premises routinely outlive the truth. A leaf blocking N rows is the highest-value row on the board: carve it out as its own small row rather than leaving it buried. Ordering is a SAFETY constraint where landing a consumer first makes the cycle permanent or ships a clean-checkout hole — say which, so it is not read as paperwork. Do not block on ordering you can fix by re-ordering.

"repo-wide green" is NOT `pnpm test`. The root vitest include has NO `apps/**`, so `pnpm test` runs ZERO tests under apps/daemon and apps/control-room. Any DoD or step note claiming repo-wide green MUST additionally run the app packages explicitly (`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`) and quote their count lines, or must say "root lane only, apps/** not covered". An architect writing a gate that touches an apps/** path must name the per-package run in the step text; a QA grading such a gate must refuse a bare `pnpm test` count line as evidence for an apps/** claim.

AT PLAN TIME, WHEN A STEP CHANGES A RETURNED SHAPE, AN EXACT KEY ROSTER, AN EXPORT SET, A LINE FORMAT, OR ADDS A CONSTANT THAT A SCANNER ENUMERATES: grep the SHAPE, not the symbol, and name every asserting consumer in the owned-path roster. A symbol grep is not sufficient and must not be the only search performed. Specifically search for: literal object/array shapes in test expectations; hard-coded counts (`expect(X.length).toBe(N)`); roster/registry files that enumerate constants by naming convention; and regexes that anchor on the format being changed. If naming every consumer would breach the row's path cap, that is a SPLIT signal at plan time — not a discovery for the worker to make at step 5. A worker who finds an unnamed consumer mid-step must stop and report rather than take the extra path, and the architect must amend or split; the worker must never rename or reformat the producer to evade the consumer's check.

SPUN-OUT ROWS. A prerequisite, leaf, successor, spinoff or sibling row created while blocked or mid-plan is filed in PLANNING (BACKLOG is human-gated and invisible to claim_next_task/wait_for_task) and MUST carry the parent id in its description and dependsOn on every consumer that waits for it (via create_task or set_task_dependencies) — sequencing is a field now, not a description sentence. Before filing, check get_context.epicSiblings: if a row already owns the capability, extend it (comment + amendment) instead of duplicating. A producer row registers its consumer edge in the same row or files the registering row before it completes — a producer with no consumer edge satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist. Only a human or governor parks to BACKLOG, with a measurable unpark condition in the reason. An epic past 40 rows is a re-slice signal for the architect (create_task warns), not a licence to keep spinning out.

EVIDENCE, SECURITY AND QUALITY WORK IS NOT ITS OWN ROW. "Security review", "add verification", "prove the acceptance criteria", "hostile coverage" filed as separate rows is the phase anti-seam wearing a compliance costume. Security tests, refusal-code assertions and hardening belong in the owning implementation row's plan and DoD; whole-epic regression, integration/e2e, the docs sweep and the adversarial pass belong in the ONE epic-final integration-and-hardening row (highest order; get_context.isEpicFinal tells you if you hold it). Per-task evidence already exists structurally: complete_task verification {command, exitCode} and completionSummary, qa_approve reviewSummary, task.commits. File a separate evidence row only when it certifies a capability shipped by a DONE row you do not own — and name that row in dependsOn. create_task warns when the epic already has a hardening row; treat the warning as a fold-in instruction, not a formality.

BLOCKING SEMANTICS (since 2026-08-29). moe.report_blocked without a resourceId frees your seat: the task keeps its blockedReason and blockedFromStatus, you are IDLE and must claim other work (the returned nextAction says so) — do not wait on your own unblock. With blockedOnTaskIds the row auto-unblocks when those rows reach DONE; a plain moe.unblock_worker only frees a seat and never clears a block — governors clear blocks with moe.set_task_status or unblock_worker {resolveBlocks:true}. Governors receive a #governors alert for blocks older than the age bound and for dep-waiting rows whose prerequisite is itself BLOCKED/BACKLOG; triage those, never re-file them. Resource blocks (resourceId) keep the old hold-and-idle behaviour because the lease grant returns the task to the same worker.

PLANNING: before submitting a plan whose DoD requires DELETING or RENAMING an exported symbol, a module, or a source line another file may assert on, the architect must enumerate every file that references it — including files that assert on SOURCE TEXT (readFileSync + toMatch/toContain against a path), not only files that import it. `git grep -l <symbol>` over the whole tree is the minimum; an import-graph walk alone misses source-text asserters because they never import what they pin. Every file found must be inside the plan's affectedFiles, or the plan must be split before submission. If the enumeration exceeds the 10-file ceiling, split — do not submit and let the worker discover it mid-flight.

A SPIDR split is NOT finished until the parent's dependsOn names its children. The splitting architect MUST either set it via moe.set_task_dependencies, or — when the seat is refused with [NOT_ALLOWED] — post an @governors request naming the parent id and the exact child id list BEFORE moe.submit_plan on the parent. A parent row left at dependsOn: [] after a split is a planning defect, not a board defect.
